description: Diplomatic transcription of the title page of each volume, line by line, with the scan. Long s as ſ; small capitals as capitals. Line styles: xl large capitals, deco decorated capitals, caps spaced capitals, s small type, it italic (<r>…</r> marks roman type inside an italic line), device a description of the printer's device, rule an ornamental rule. Read from the scans; checked against them by eye.

lines: Appliqués à la conduite & aux affaires des nations
Nihil eſt enim illi principi Deo, qui omnem hunc mundum regit, quod
quidem in terris fiat, acceptius, quam concilia cœtusque hominum
jure ſociati, quæ civitates appellantur. <r>CICER. Somn. Scipion.</r>
[Printer's device: two clasped hands holding a staff with a cap of liberty; scroll: APUD LIBEROS TUTIOR]
De l'Imprimerie de la Société Typographique.
Appliqués à la conduite & aux affaires des Nations
Nihil eſt enim illi principi Deo, qui omnem hunc mundum regit, quod
quidem in terris fiat, acceptius, quam conſilia cœtuſque hominum
jure ſociati, quæ civitates appellantur. <r>CICER. Somn. Scipion.</r>
[Printer's device: two clasped hands holding a staff with a cap of liberty; scroll: APUD LIBEROS TUTIOR]
De l'Imprimerie de la Société Typographique.

notes: The two volumes differ: T1 prints "nations", "ſouverains", "concilia cœtusque", "A NEUCHATEL." and "M. DCC. LXXIII."; T2 prints "Nations", "Souverains", "conſilia cœtuſque", "A NEUCHATEL," and "M. DCC. LXXIII,". Cicero's text (De re publica VI.13) reads concilia.
